title: Drift and the rules of rebalancing
objectives: Show how a market move creates drift.
State the rebalancing rules to agree with the client in writing.
body_md:
Markets move the mix on their own. Rebalancing brings it back, and in doing so it quietly sells high and buys low.

## How drift happens

Starting at 60/40 equity/debt:

| After a year when… | Equity share becomes | Rebalancing means |
|---|---|---|
| Equity +30%, debt +7% | ≈ 65% | Move about 5 points from equity to debt (book some gains) |
| Equity −25%, debt +7% | ≈ 51% | Move about 9 points from debt to equity (buy after the fall) |

## The rules to agree in writing

- Calendar rule: check once a year on a fixed date.
- Band rule: act when any asset class drifts more than 5 percentage points from target (10 for smaller portfolios).
- Use new money first: direct fresh SIPs or lump sums to the underweight asset before selling anything.
- Check costs before selling: exit loads and capital-gains tax. Refer tax to a CA.

## Why rules beat judgement

A rule tells the client in advance what will happen after a big year, in both directions. That is what makes rebalancing acceptable, especially when it means adding to the asset that just fell.
example: A 60/40 portfolio ends a strong year at 65/35. The band rule triggers at 5 points, so about 5 points move from equity to debt — booking gains, not predicting a fall.
say: Rebalancing is going back to the mix we agreed, not a prediction about the market.
Before we sell anything, let's use the new SIP money for the underweight part.
never: Let's sell equity because a fall is coming.

talk_track.title: Markets move the mix; rebalancing brings it back
talk_track.text: Markets move the mix on their own. Start with a sixty-forty target. After a year when equity rises thirty percent and debt seven, equity becomes about sixty-five percent. Rebalancing means moving about five points back to debt, booking some gains. After a year when equity falls twenty-five percent, equity drops to about fifty-one percent. Rebalancing means moving about nine points from debt into equity, buying after the fall. Agree the rules in writing.

check.q: A 60/40 portfolio becomes 65/35 after a strong equity year. What does rebalancing involve?
o: Moving about 5 points from equity to debt
check.why: Return to target by booking some equity gains.

check.q: What is usually the cheapest way to rebalance?
o: Directing new money to the underweight asset
check.why: New money avoids exit loads and tax on a sale.

check.q: What happens after a year when equity falls 25% and debt gains 7%?
o: Equity becomes about 51%, so rebalancing buys equity after the fall
Equity becomes 65%, so we sell equity
check.why: Equity drifts down to about 51%, so rebalancing moves about 9 points from debt into equity.
